stories.title: Apple unveils M5 Ultra and M6 chips
stories.summary: Apple introduced two new chips: the M5 Ultra and the M6. Apple calls them its most powerful chips yet. The chips will likely power upcoming Mac models.
stories.whyItMatters: Apple's chip design sets the pace for its whole Mac lineup and its position against rival chipmakers.

Independent performance benchmarks

questions: How much of the improvement targets AI workloads versus general tasks?

stories.title: Apple's new desktop Macs target local AI development
stories.summary: Apple introduced new desktop computers built for local AI development. The machines let developers do AI work on the device itself. This follows Apple's push into more powerful in-house chips.
stories.whyItMatters: The move shows Apple courting AI developers directly, an area now dominated by cloud computing providers.
whatToWatch: Specs and pricing for the new machines
Adoption among AI developers
How the hardware pairs with Apple's new M5 Ultra and M6 chips

stories.title: Instagram tests 'First Draft' to auto-trim Reels clips
stories.summary: Instagram launched a feature called First Draft. It automatically trims Reels clips for creators. Meta says this cuts down on tedious manual editing.
stories.whyItMatters: The feature lowers the effort needed to make short video, a key front in Meta's competition with TikTok for creators.
whatToWatch: Wider rollout beyond the initial test
Creator feedback on the automatic edits
questions: How much control do creators keep over the AI-trimmed clips?

stories.title: Nothing OS 5.0 adds a Glyph Interface app and more homescreen options
stories.summary: Nothing released OS 5.0 for its phones. The update adds a dedicated Glyph Interface app. It also adds more ways to customize the homescreen.
stories.whyItMatters: Nothing competes on software design, not just specs, and this update pushes further into that lane inside the Android market.
whatToWatch: Rollout timeline across Nothing devices

stories.title: X sends cease-and-desist to open-source Twitter viewer Nitter
stories.summary: X sent a cease-and-desist letter to Nitter, an open-source project. X alleges Nitter scraped its platform without permission. Nitter lets people view X posts without an account.
stories.whyItMatters: The action fits a pattern of platforms shutting out third-party tools, which narrows open access to social data.
whatToWatch: Whether Nitter shuts down or changes how it operates
Any legal action beyond the letter
questions: What is the legal basis for X's scraping claim?
Will other open-source viewers face the same action?

stories.title: Apple reverses plan to weaken Hide My Email
stories.summary: Apple decided to keep its Hide My Email feature intact. Apple had earlier moved to undermine the privacy tool. Hide My Email lets users sign up for services with a masked address.
stories.whyItMatters: The reversal tests Apple's privacy-first brand and shows it will walk back changes under pushback.
whatToWatch: An official Apple explanation of the reversal
Whether related changes also get rolled back
questions: What prompted Apple to undermine the feature in the first place?

stories.title: Self-driving truck startup Gatik raises $200M after PepsiCo deal
stories.summary: Gatik, a startup that builds self-driving trucks for short-haul freight, raised $200 million. The round follows a deal with PepsiCo. Gatik focuses on shorter, repeatable delivery routes.
stories.whyItMatters: The raise shows investors still back autonomous freight, even as parts of the wider self-driving industry consolidate.
whatToWatch: How Gatik uses the new funding
Growth of the PepsiCo partnership
New retail or logistics partners
questions: What is Gatik's path to profitability?

stories.title: Google's Pixel 11 Pro Fold improves, but doesn't lead the foldable market
stories.summary: Wired reviewed Google's Pixel 11 Pro Fold and called it better than before, but not the best foldable available. The review points to steady, not dramatic, progress in Google's foldable line.
stories.whyItMatters: Foldables are a test of Google's hardware ambitions against Samsung, and incremental gains suggest the category is maturing slowly.
whatToWatch: Sales performance of the Pixel 11 Pro Fold
Samsung's response with its own foldable line
questions: What specifically keeps the Pixel Fold from leading the category?

stories.title: Google rolls out anti-nausea 'Motion Assist' dots on Android
stories.summary: Google is rolling out a feature called Motion Assist on Android. It shows moving dots on screen to reduce motion sickness. The rollout comes after the feature was announced earlier.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows platform makers investing in comfort and accessibility, not just speed or camera specs.
whatToWatch: Which devices get the feature first
User reaction once it reaches more phones

stories.title: When you should turn off Find My iPhone
stories.summary: A guide explains when to turn off Apple's Find My iPhone feature. Common reasons include selling or transferring a device, or addressing personal safety concerns. The feature is normally left on for theft recovery.
stories.whyItMatters: It highlights how device-tracking features cut both ways: useful for recovery, but a risk if misused for monitoring someone.

stories.title: Andy Dunn's Pie shifts from events app to social network
stories.summary: Pie, the startup from Bonobos co-founder Andy Dunn, is moving away from being mainly an events app. It is becoming more of a general social network. The shift marks a change in the app's core focus.
stories.whyItMatters: It reflects ongoing experimentation by founders looking for a social app format that can grow beyond incumbents like Instagram and X.

User growth after the shift
questions: How will Pie differentiate itself from existing social apps?

stories.summary: TechCrunch is asking readers to vote on which Audience Choice sessions appear at its Founder Summit. The vote lets the audience help shape part of the event's agenda.
stories.whyItMatters: It matters mainly to founders and investors planning to attend the summit.
